questions.question: At what blood alcohol concentration is everyone's driving impaired?
questions.explanation: Everyone's driving is impaired at a BAC of 0.08 percent, although many people are affected at much lower levels.
questions.sourceQuote: Everyone’s driving is impaired at a blood alcohol concentration, or BAC, of 0.08 percent

questions.question: Research shows the risk of being involved in a crash increases when the alcohol level reaches what percentage?
questions.explanation: The risk of being involved in a crash increases at 0.05 percent, and at 0.08 percent the risk of causing a fatal crash is even greater.
questions.sourceQuote: the risk of being involved in a crash increases when the alcohol level is 0.05 percent

questions.question: In what year did the North Carolina General Assembly enact the Safe Roads Act?
questions.explanation: The Safe Roads Act was enacted in 1983.
questions.sourceQuote: In 1983, the North Carolina General Assembly enacted the Safe Roads Act.

questions.question: What did the Safe Roads Act do?
choices: Lowered the legal drinking age to 18
Created the state's first commercial driver license program
Repealed all previous drunk driving laws and replaced them with a single offense of Driving While Impaired
Required ignition interlock devices on all new vehicles
questions.explanation: The act repealed all previous drunk driving laws and replaced them with one offense, Driving While Impaired, or DWI.
questions.sourceQuote: This act repealed all previous laws on drunk driving in North Carolina and replaced them with a single offense

questions.question: If an officer charges you with driving while impaired, you will be asked to take a chemical test of what?
questions.explanation: A person charged with DWI is asked to take a chemical test of their breath or blood.
questions.sourceQuote: you will be asked to take a chemical test of your breath or blood

questions.question: If you refuse to perform a required chemical test, your driver license will be revoked immediately for at least how long?
questions.explanation: Refusal to perform a required test results in immediate revocation of your driver license for at least 30 days.
questions.sourceQuote: Refusal to perform any required test will result in the immediate revocation of your driver license for at least 30 days

questions.question: Besides the immediate revocation, what additional revocation does the DMV impose for refusing a required chemical test?
questions.explanation: A refusal also brings an additional, minimum 12-month revocation by the DMV.
questions.sourceQuote: and an additional, minimum 12-month revocation by the DMV

questions.question: After how many months of the willful refusal revocation have elapsed may a judge issue a limited driving privilege?
questions.explanation: In certain instances, after six months of the willful refusal revocation has elapsed, the judge may issue a limited driving privilege.
questions.sourceQuote: after six months of the willful refusal revocation has elapsed, the judge may issue a limited driving privilege

questions.question: If your chemical test shows a BAC of 0.08 percent or more, your driving privilege will be revoked immediately for a minimum of what period?
questions.explanation: A test result of 0.08 percent or more (0.04 or more in a commercial motor vehicle) brings immediate revocation for a minimum of 30 days.
questions.sourceQuote: your driving privilege will be revoked immediately for a minimum of 30 days

questions.question: What BAC level is the impaired driving threshold when you are driving a commercial motor vehicle?
questions.explanation: For a commercial motor vehicle the threshold is 0.04 or more, lower than the 0.08 limit for other drivers.
questions.sourceQuote: 0.08 percent or more (0.04 or more, if you are driving a commercial motor vehicle)

questions.question: Besides proving a BAC of 0.08 percent or more, how else can driving while impaired be proven?
choices: By proving the driver was speeding
By proving the driver failed a road sign test
By proving the driver had an open container
By proving the driver's physical or mental fitness are appreciably impaired by alcohol, drugs, or a combination of both
questions.explanation: DWI can be proven either by impairment of the driver's physical or mental fitness by alcohol, drugs or a combination of both, or by BAC of 0.08 percent or more.
questions.sourceQuote: the driver's physical or mental fitness are appreciably impaired by alcohol, drugs or a combination of both

questions.question: What may be used as evidence in court in a DWI case?
choices: The results of your chemical test or the fact that you refused to take the test
Only statements made to the officer at the stop
questions.explanation: The results of your chemical test or the fact that you refused to take the test are admissible as evidence in court.
questions.sourceQuote: the results of your chemical test or the fact that you refused to take the test will be admissible as evidence in court

questions.question: Which practice do North Carolina DWI laws allow enforcement agencies to use?
choices: Road blocks to check for impaired drivers
Immediate vehicle forfeiture at any speeding stop
questions.explanation: DWI laws allow enforcement agencies to set up road blocks to check for impaired drivers.
questions.sourceQuote: Allow enforcement agencies to set up road blocks to check for impaired drivers

questions.question: Under North Carolina DWI laws, what are drivers prohibited from doing while driving?
choices: Consuming any alcoholic beverage, including beer
Carrying a closed container in the trunk
Having passengers who have been drinking
questions.explanation: Drivers are prohibited from consuming any alcoholic beverage, including beer, while driving.
questions.sourceQuote: Prohibit drivers from consuming any alcoholic beverage, including beer, while driving

questions.question: What does North Carolina law say about transporting an open container of an alcoholic beverage?
choices: It is prohibited, including in the passenger area of the car
It is allowed if the container is on the floor
It is allowed if the container is less than half full
It is allowed for passengers 21 and older
questions.explanation: The transport of an open container of any alcoholic beverage is prohibited, including in the passenger area of the car.
questions.sourceQuote: Prohibit the transport of an open container of any alcoholic beverage, including in the passenger area of the car

questions.question: In a commercial motor vehicle, what is prohibited in the passenger area while on any highway, street, or public vehicular area?
choices: Possession of alcoholic beverages, open or closed
Nothing; commercial vehicle rules do not cover alcohol
questions.explanation: It is against the law to possess alcoholic beverages, open or closed, in the passenger area of a commercial motor vehicle on any highway, street, or public vehicular area.
questions.sourceQuote: Prohibit the possession of alcoholic beverages (open or closed) in the passenger area of a commercial motor vehicle

questions.question: What does North Carolina DWI law require of a person convicted of DWI for the second time?
choices: Installation of an ignition interlock on every family vehicle
questions.explanation: Persons convicted of DWI for the second time are required to serve a jail sentence.
questions.sourceQuote: Require persons who are convicted of DWI for the second time to serve a jail sentence

questions.question: What must anyone convicted of DWI obtain before driving privileges are reinstated?
questions.explanation: Anyone convicted of DWI must obtain a substance abuse assessment prior to the reinstatement of driving privileges.
questions.sourceQuote: Require anyone convicted of DWI to obtain a substance abuse assessment prior to the reinstatement of driving privileges

questions.question: Under North Carolina DWI laws, what are persons with lower BACs required to attend?
choices: A defensive driving clinic for commercial drivers
questions.explanation: DWI laws require persons with lower BACs to attend alcohol safety schools.
questions.sourceQuote: Require persons with lower BACs to attend alcohol safety schools

questions.question: If you are convicted of DWI while your license is revoked for an earlier DWI conviction, what may the court do?
choices: Order your vehicle seized and sold
questions.explanation: The court may order your vehicle seized and sold when you are convicted of DWI while your license is already revoked for an earlier DWI conviction.
questions.sourceQuote: the court may order your vehicle seized and sold

questions.question: What is the mandatory driver license revocation period for a first DWI conviction?
questions.explanation: A first DWI conviction brings mandatory revocation of your driver license for one year.
questions.sourceQuote: First conviction: Mandatory revocation of your driver license for a period of one year.

questions.question: A second DWI conviction brings a mandatory four-year revocation when the prior offense occurred within what period of the current offense?
questions.explanation: The four-year revocation for a second conviction applies when the prior offense occurred within three years of the current offense.
questions.sourceQuote: Mandatory driver license revocation for a period of four years when convicted of a prior offense which occurred within three years

questions.question: A third DWI conviction brings mandatory permanent license revocation if at least one prior conviction occurred within what period?
questions.explanation: A third conviction means mandatory permanent revocation if at least one of the prior convictions occurred within the past five years.
questions.sourceQuote: Mandatory, permanent driver license revocation if at least one of the prior convictions occurred within the past five years.

questions.question: A fourth DWI conviction is considered a felony if the three prior DWI convictions occurred within what period?
questions.explanation: A fourth conviction is a felony when the three prior DWI convictions occurred within the past seven years.
questions.sourceQuote: The fourth conviction is considered a felony if the three prior DWI convictions occurred within the past seven years.

questions.question: On the first restoration of a license after a DWI suspension, what is the required alcohol concentration restriction?
questions.explanation: On the first restoration, the alcohol concentration restriction is 0.04.
questions.sourceQuote: On the first restoration, the alcohol concentration restriction will be 0.04.

questions.question: What is the alcohol concentration restriction on a second or subsequent restoration after a DWI suspension?
questions.explanation: On a second or subsequent restoration, the alcohol concentration restriction is 0.00.
questions.sourceQuote: On a second or subsequent restoration, the alcohol concentration restriction will be 0.00.

questions.question: A DWI conviction with a BAC of 0.15 or more, or another conviction within the past seven years, requires what?
choices: An ignition interlock device installed on the vehicle
questions.explanation: A conviction with a BAC of 0.15 or more, or another conviction within the past seven years, requires an ignition interlock device on the vehicle.
questions.sourceQuote: 0.15 or more, or another conviction within the past seven years, will require an ignition interlock device to be installed on the vehicle.

questions.question: What is the legal age to purchase any alcoholic beverage in North Carolina?
questions.explanation: The legal age to purchase any alcoholic beverage in North Carolina is 21.
questions.sourceQuote: The legal age to purchase any alcoholic beverage in North Carolina is 21.

questions.question: A driver who is less than 21 years old and convicted of driving with any amount of alcohol or drugs in their body will have their license revoked for what period?
questions.explanation: A driver under 21 convicted of driving with any amount of alcohol or drugs in their body loses their license for one year.
questions.sourceQuote: is convicted for an offense of driving with any amount of alcohol or drugs in their body, their license will be revoked for one year.

questions.question: Which of the following results in a one-year driver license revocation?
choices: Giving an alcoholic beverage to an underage person
Riding as a passenger with a driver who has an open container
Allowing a 25-year-old friend to use your license
questions.explanation: The one-year revocation applies to any person who gives an alcoholic beverage to an underage person, along with several underage purchase and fraudulent ID offenses.
questions.sourceQuote: Any person who gives an alcoholic beverage to any underage person.
